=== MUTATION PROBES (deliberately breaking what this PR's checks guard) ===
A vacuous check is one that still passes when you break what it guards. I broke three things:

P1. HANDOFF.md generated block, "24/24 proven" -> "25/25 proven".
    `scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .` EXIT 1:
      "FAIL: HANDOFF.md:54: [stale deliverable proof state in generated block] recorded=['25/25 proven', ...] re-derived=['24/24 proven', ...]"
    Not vacuous: it re-derives the count from proof/ rather than pattern-matching the text.
    NOTE, worth knowing: `scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check` stayed EXIT 0 on the same corruption -- it is a SHAPE check only, and the count is state-claims' job. Correct division of labour, but do not read a green handoff-shape step as evidence the count is right.

P2. proof record `"pr": 71` -> `"pr": 70` (i.e. the exact self-consistent-looking lie the filename cannot catch, since this file is slug-named and `_authoritative_pr_from_filename` returns None for it).
    `scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 71 --base <base> --head <head>` EXIT 1, two distinct failures:
      "PR #71 carries no proof/*.json record for itself"
      "...is new in this PR but self-declares 'pr' (70) instead of 71 (this PR's actual number, known to CI independent of anything the record or its filename claims)"
    Not vacuous, and it closes the gap its own docstring admits the filename check cannot.

P3. ORDERING TRAP, checked explicitly because it is the shape that has gone red here before. 389e920 adds the proof record AND regenerates the HANDOFF block in one commit; 965832f then edits that proof record again, AFTER the generator ran. If `pr` participated in the proven/total count, the block would be stale one commit later.
    Measured both ends: `lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .` EXIT 0 at 389e920 AND EXIT 0 at the tip 965832f. The tip's edit changes a field, not the record count, so the generator does not need to be re-run. NO ordering defect here.

=== THE WRONG-SECRET-NAME TRAP: CHECKED, AND IT RESOLVES ===
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` reads `${{ secrets.LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES }}`. A secret referenced under a name the repo does not have expands to the empty string silently. I could not read the repository's secret list (no admin scope on this token), so I resolved it the other way, from observed behaviour: the check now FAILS CLOSED on an empty/unset value (measured directly above, EXIT 1), and CI's "lwb-env-leak" and "lwb-env-leak-history" steps are BOTH `success` on this exact head. A green fail-closed check is only reachable with a non-empty value, so the name in the workflow is a name the repository actually has. This is the "I could not check" / "I checked and found nothing" distinction the brief warns about: I could not read the secret list, and I am not pretending otherwise -- I substituted a different measurement that answers the same question.

=== PROCESS FINDING, NOT A FINDING AGAINST THIS PR ===
My dispatch instruction says to skip a PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA. Applied literally that rule matches nothing in this repo, ever: committing a record advances the head past the sha the record names, which is the exact problem `resolve_reviewable_head` exists to solve. Following it literally, I would have re-reviewed all 14 open PRs and appended 14 redundant record commits. I computed `resolve_reviewable_head` for every open PR instead: 13 of 14 (#45, #46, #51, #53, #58, #60, #61, #62, #63, #64, #66, #68, #69) already carry an AGREE naming their reviewable head and needed nothing. #71 was the only genuinely unreviewed PR, and is the only one I touched. The skip criterion should read "reviewable head", not "head".
Second-order observation on the same mechanism, recorded not resolved: because verdicts pin to the reviewable head, a commit touching only proof/ -- such as this branch's tip 965832f, which edited a proof record's contents -- is by construction never named by any review record. proof/ records are evidence documents, not pure bookkeeping. Narrow, deliberate in the design, and a property of main's lwb_lanes.py rather than of this PR; I name it so it is a known residual rather than a surprise.
